vision: A distributable library of AI coding assistant rules, skills, hooks, and a file-based harness for Cursor and Claude Code. THE HARNESS IS: a durable, file-system task system that keeps AI agents honest across sessions. It solves five problems the owner identified: (1) repository scope — vision, direction, trade-offs in state.json; (2) task definition — discrete tasks with type and scope; (3) task grouping — flat tasks[] array filtered by status at read time; (4) task status tracking — lifecycle enum + append-only breadcrumbs.jsonl for session recovery; (5) acceptance criteria — contract.json with binary-testable criteria negotiated before implementation. For whom: teams using Cursor/Claude Code on non-trivial multi-file work who need agents to stop self-grading and stop losing context between sessions. Why each component exists: state.json = scope + backlog; contract.json = definition of done; breadcrumbs = audit trail; planner subagent = decompose vague requests; evaluator subagent = adversarial QA separate from builder context; hooks (lean) = enforce contract-before-code structurally; eval pipeline = regression test that agents follow the workflow. HONEST ASSESSMENT: the core five-problem harness is sound and ~40 lines of JSON + rules. Everything layered on top — negotiations/ JSON schemas, 11 hooks (full profile), metrics dashboard, 41 scenario evals with 5 judge tiers, multi-agent orchestration, UI dashboard — has grown organically and now obscures the value proposition. 47 verified tasks prove the core works; 13 pending tasks are mostly eval-tooling bugs and nice-to-haves, not harness failures.
direction: POST SPIKE-EVAL-RESEARCH (2026-06-03): spike-eval-research VERIFIED — surveyed SWE-bench, AgentBench, Inspect AI, METR, Braintrust, LangSmith, trajscore, trajectly, Anthropic eval guide. Key findings: (1) deterministic trajectory checks are industry standard and we lack them, (2) LLM judge needs calibration against golden set, (3) default return True in behavioral heuristics silently hides failures, (4) rule ablation via paired comparison is standard for measuring rule effectiveness. NEW TASKS: feat-14a (LLM judge Phase A: calibration + UNKNOWN + smart truncation), feat-15 (trajectory tier), feat-16 (rule ablation), chore-uncertain-elimination (kill return True default), gap-26 (heuristic dedup). feat-14 CANCELLED in favor of phased feat-14a. REMAINING: gap-14 session boundary (33%), gap-18 skip-harness auth (57%), chore-archive-review. ARCHITECTURE unchanged: structural deny for critical steps, advisory for quality signals.

trade_offs.decision: Flat tasks array, not grouped buckets
trade_offs.reasoning: Hooks and agents iterate one list today; grouped buckets duplicate items and drift. harness-context.sh can filter by status at read time.
Eight lean hooks, harness_lint.py, and 20 eval scenarios already encode this lifecycle. done conflates verified and committed; doing conflates building and evaluating.

trade_offs.decision: Explicit type enum on every task
trade_offs.alternative: Infer type from id prefix only (feat-/gap-/spike-)
trade_offs.reasoning: Id prefixes are convention not validation; explicit type enables lint enforcement and clearer planner output.
22+ eval scenario seeds and 6 shell hooks read features today; alias prevents eval regression during phased rollout.
Preserves audit trail; metrics exclude cancelled from backlog counts.

trade_offs.alternative: Keep symlinks tracked, gitignore only transient files
trade_offs.reasoning: Matches how consumer projects treat IDE config; library/cursor/ is the distributable artifact
spec.md was read once (plan gate) then became stale. Single file eliminates drift by design.

trade_offs.alternative: Build evaluator chaining and parallel evaluators
trade_offs.reasoning: Manual /evaluator launch works. Orchestration adds complexity for a problem (evaluator doesn't run) already solved by chain-evaluator.sh hook and rules. No user demand.
state.json and breadcrumbs are human-readable JSON. Dashboard solves a problem that doesn't exist yet. metrics.json is broken anyway (gap-21).

trade_offs.decision: Defer feat-14 LLM-as-judge until after schema consolidation
trade_offs.alternative: Build LLM judge now to fix UNCERTAIN verdicts
trade_offs.reasoning: 89.8% mean is acceptable. Many UNCERTAIN/FAIL are judge bugs (gap-20 harness_level placement, gap-19 heuristics), not agent failures. Fix tooling before adding LLM cost.
Eval accuracy issues are symptoms of schema drift and inconsistent harness_level placement across 41 scenarios. Consolidation fixes root cause.

trade_offs.decision: Keep lean hook profile as default; demote full profile
trade_offs.reasoning: Lean (4 hooks) enforces the five-problem core. Full profile adds dedup-server, context-health, evaluator-guard, harness-gate LLM routing — valuable for this repo's dogfooding, optional for consumers.

trade_offs.alternative: Enforce structured negotiation JSON per HARNESS_STANDARD.md
trade_offs.reasoning: negotiations/ directory is rarely populated in practice. Breadcrumbs with type=negotiate capture the same signal with less schema burden. HARNESS_STANDARD over-specifies this artifact.

trade_offs.decision: Decompose spike-eval-research into 6 sequential research phases
trade_offs.reasoning: Four distinct eval dimensions (rules, skills, trajectory, LLM judge) plus baseline inventory and synthesis need focused research passes. Sequential phases produce partial notes that roll into one spike doc without scope creep into implementation.

open_questions: Should negotiations/ folder be deprecated in favor of negotiate-type breadcrumbs only?
Is full hook profile worth maintaining for consumer projects, or ship lean-only?
What is the minimum eval scenario set that protects the five-problem core? Target: 12-15 protocol scenarios.
Should contract.json phase enum add 'verified' explicitly (used in practice, missing from HARNESS_STANDARD.md)?
Does gap-14 need feat-14 LLM judge, or stronger planning_discipline.mdc enforcement?
Can rule/skill A/B scenarios run in our worktree-based session_runner without doubling eval cost?
Should trajectory scoring be deterministic (tool-call graph) or LLM-only (feat-14 path)?

tasks.name: Session boundary at 33% — agent does not suggest fresh thread or checkpoint
tasks.details: AUDIT: REAL but NOT harness-core. behavioral_session_boundary 33% (was 70%). Agent behavior gap, not missing infrastructure. Fix path: strengthen planning_discipline.mdc + agent_behavior opener (not feat-14 LLM judge, not new hooks). Deprioritized P1→P2: session hygiene is nice-to-have; contract-gate and acceptance criteria are essential.

tasks.name: LLM-as-judge for post_hoc_rubric
tasks.details: SUPERSEDED by feat-14a (phased approach from spike-eval-research). feat-14a covers calibration set + UNKNOWN verdict + smart truncation + per-dimension rubrics as Phase A. Original feat-14 scope was too broad and lacked calibration prerequisite.

tasks.name: adversarial_skip_override at 57% — auth implementation incomplete under skip-harness
tasks.details: AUDIT: REAL agent failure, NOT harness over-engineering. Agent skips harness correctly but doesn't finish JWT auth. Deprioritized P2→P3: tests agent coding under skip-harness, not the five-problem core. May be timeout (300s). Fix: extend scenario timeout or narrow auth scope in seed.

tasks.name: Research evaluation frameworks for rules, skills, and agent trajectory
tasks.details: COMPLETE. Deliverable: .harness/docs/spike-eval-research.md (6 sections). Surveyed SWE-bench, AgentBench, Inspect AI, METR, Braintrust, LangSmith, trajscore, trajectly, Anthropic eval guide. Proposed 6 follow-up tasks: feat-14a (LLM judge calibration), feat-15 (trajectory tier), feat-16 (rule ablation), chore-uncertain-elimination, chore-skill-scenarios, gap-26 (heuristic dedup). Key findings: (1) deterministic trajectory checks are standard and we lack them, (2) LLM judge needs calibration against golden set before any improvement, (3) default return True in behavioral heuristics silently hides failures, (4) rule ablation via paired comparison is the standard for measuring rule effectiveness.

tasks.name: LLM judge Phase A: calibration set + UNKNOWN verdict + smart truncation + per-dimension rubrics
tasks.details: From spike-eval-research. Phase A of feat-14 redesign: (1) Build golden calibration set of 30-50 human-labeled session transcripts across negotiation_quality and trajectory_quality criteria, (2) Add UNKNOWN verdict to judge_with_llm() for insufficient evidence, (3) Smart truncation: extract first turn + tool calls + errors + harness interactions + last turn instead of head-truncating to 8KB, (4) Per-dimension rubric prompts with anchor examples (1 PASS, 1 FAIL per dimension), (5) Confidence thresholding: confidence < 3 → UNCERTAIN. Measure Cohen's κ against golden set before/after changes.

tasks.name: Trajectory tier: deterministic tool-call checks in session_judge.py
tasks.details: From spike-eval-research. Add trajectory tier between structural and LLM in session_judge.py. Deterministic checks: (1) loop detection — repeated identical tool calls (same name + args) > 2 consecutive, (2) step efficiency — total tool calls vs difficulty-adjusted range, (3) read-before-write — verify Read before Write/StrReplace on same file, (4) skeleton matching — required tool-call subsequence from scenario YAML trajectory_skeleton field, (5) backtracking ratio — StrReplace(same file)/total edits, (6) idle detection — consecutive responses without tool calls, (7) error recovery — Shell non-zero exit → next action addresses it within 3 steps. Inspired by trajscore and trajectly.

tasks.name: Rule ablation mode in session_runner.py for paired A/B comparison
tasks.details: From spike-eval-research. Add --ablate-rule flag to session_runner.py. Runs each scenario twice: with full .cursor/rules/ and with target rule removed. session_judge scores both sessions. Report per-criterion delta, aggregate delta, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Cohen's d effect size. Priority rules to ablate: adversarial_harness.mdc, autonomous_execution.mdc, progress_tracking.mdc, planning_discipline.mdc.

tasks.name: Kill default return True in _evaluate_behavioral(); require explicit handling
tasks.details: COMPLETE. Replaced default return True with return None → UNMATCHED sentinel. Added 10 new behavioral branches + broadened 6 existing to cover all 87 corpus criteria (0 fallthroughs). check_behavioral maps None→UNMATCHED result with warning. judge_session tracks unmatched count separately. session_report counts UNMATCHED in dimensions and aggregate. Regression tests in tests/eval/test_session_judge_behavioral.py. Evaluator: PASS 9/9 AC + 4/4 EC (round 2).

tasks.name: Behavioral heuristic dedup and fragility reduction in session_judge.py
tasks.details: From spike-eval-research. _evaluate_behavioral() has 26 branches with duplicates and high-fragility patterns. (1) Merge branches 4/5 (both check proceed_patterns) and 19/21 (both check response < 800 words), (2) Reduce false-positive surface of high-fragility branches 10 (off-plan, 20+ regex alternatives), 13 (proactively updated, indirect signal), 16/17 (session boundary, overlapping patterns), (3) Tighten default fallback per chore-uncertain-elimination.

tasks.name: Create 2-3 scenarios with skill_activation rubric to test skill quality
tasks.details: From spike-eval-research. check_skill_activation() exists in session_judge.py but no scenario uses skill_activation rubric. SDK bridge doesn't auto-route skills, so agent must proactively read SKILL.md. Create 2-3 scenarios that seed task descriptions matching skill keywords, then check whether agent reads the skill file and follows instructions. Tests skill quality (does the skill produce better output?), not routing (IDE concern).

tasks.name: Add verification that archived tasks are actually complete before archiving
tasks.details: archive-tasks.py trusts status field blindly. Add checks: (1) verified tasks should have an eval report or breadcrumb with result=pass, (2) cancelled tasks should have a reason in details field, (3) warn/block if a verified task has no eval evidence. Prevents premature archiving of tasks marked done without actual verification.
